summary: The corroboration audit of 24 key details from Brendan Dassey’s interrogations shows that investigators introduced 8 details first, the suspect introduced 11 first, 4 were already public before any interview, and 1 may trace to an earlier unrecorded statement. One detail (tattoo on stomach) was raised by investigators but never adopted by the suspect. Across three recorded sessions, interrogators dominated the dialogue and repeatedly used tactics such as “we already know” (52 times) and “demand truth” (85 times).
key_points: 8 of 24 key details were first stated by investigators (e.g., vehicle in garage, tied with rope, stabbed in stomach, throat cut, shot in head, shot in garage, blood on floor, body burned) — cited from investigator statements at Feb 27 Mishicot High School, p. fassbender/wiegert and Mar 1 Manitowoc, p. wiegert.

11 details originated with the suspect (e.g., knife, restrained on bed, strangled, hair cut, .22 rifle, tires/branches on fire, RAV4 hidden, hood raised, bedsheets burned, phone/camera/purse burned, bones broken) — cited from suspect statements at Feb 27 Mishicot High School, p. brendan and Mar 1 Manitowoc, p. brendan.

4 details were publicly reported before any interview (body burned, license plates removed, vehicle key in bedroom, clothes burned) — cited from public reports Nov 10/16, 2005 noted in Mar 1 Manitowoc, p. brendan and Feb 27 Mishicot, p. fassbender/wiegert.
1 detail (bleach on jeans) may trace to an earlier unrecorded statement with Fassbender on the evening of Feb 27, 2006 — cited from Decision and Order p. 7, citing ECF 19-19 at 10-11.
1 detail (tattoo on stomach) was raised by investigators but never adopted by the suspect — cited from May 13 Sheboygan, p. fassbender.

Interrogation dynamics: Session 1 (Feb 27) interrogators spoke 91.7% of words, suspect gave 76 minimal answers; Session 2 (Mar 1) interrogators 68.4%, 594 minimal answers; Session 3 (May 13) interrogators 73.3%, 378 minimal answers — cited from session data S1, S2, S3.
limits: This audit only tracks where details appear in the available transcripts; it cannot assess truthfulness or reliability of any detail.
Two sessions (Feb 27 evening with Fassbender, Feb 27 Two Rivers PD) have no public transcript, so possible earlier disclosures are not fully captured.
The audit does not evaluate whether the suspect’s adoption of investigator-introduced details resulted from suggestion, coercion, or independent knowledge.
No assessment of the suspect’s mental state, comprehension, or voluntariness is included.
